correctness.rationale: Every active pair bounds its ordinary endpoint-degree sum. Summation gives sum d_i^2<=T(T-k), Cauchy gives 4T^2/n<=sum d_i^2, yielding T>=n(n-1)/4. By complement symmetry also T<=that bound. Equality forces each d_i=(n-1)/2. Integrality excludes n=0 mod4; for n=1 mod4 exact local counts h and h-1 prove sufficiency of regular graphs. Direct exhaustive n=5 and independent formula-vs-adjacency checks support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The Kneser disjointness graphs form a canonical vertex-transitive family. The exact infinite-family equilibrium classification is forced by a sharp extremal quadratic degree inequality. A residue-0 graph has consensus-only fixed points whereas a residue-1 graph has an explicit bijection with highly structured half-regular graphs, a mathematically motivated abrupt contrast. The explicit coefficient count encodes all labelled equilibria, not a small arbitrary computation.
